Scientists estimate over 180,000 giant tortoises live on one Seychelles island

A new study estimates that adult and subadult Aldabra giant tortoises roam freely across Aldabra Atoll, far outnumbering its human population https://t.co/KP8YjCxWc4

Aldabra Atoll holds roughly 180,000 giant tortoises, a new count shows, outnumbering the entire human population of the Seychelles and marking one of conservation's most successful wildlife recoveries.

🐢 Good news for conservation: Aldabra's giant tortoise population hits a record high! 🐢

A remote island in Seychelles is home to more giant tortoises than ever recorded. The latest survey, led by the Seychelles Islands Foundation (SIF) and the University of Exeter, has found roughly 180,000 Aldabra giant tortoises living on Aldabra Atoll. That is the highest figure ever recorded for the species, and it far exceeds the human population of Seychelles itself! 🌴

How did they count them?
Researchers analysed five years of tortoise counts, from 2018 to 2022. It is the first update since the widely cited figure of 100,000, which dates back to the late 1990s. The study, published in the journal Ecology and Evolution, puts the best estimate at almost 183,000 adult and sub-adult tortoises, and found the population was relatively stable over the period.

Why does this matter?
Aldabra is one of only two places on Earth where giant tortoises still live in the wild. The other is the Galápagos, which has a much smaller population. That makes Aldabra's thriving tortoises all the more precious. 🌍

Dr Frauke Fleischer-Dogley, CEO of SIF, said that more than 180,000 giant tortoises roaming freely on the atoll is proof of what long-term commitment to conservation can achieve. She called it wonderful news for Seychelles, for the world, and for everyone who has worked to protect Aldabra. 💚

In a time when so much environmental news is worrying, this is a reminder that dedicated, long-term conservation really works.

publications.title: Giant tortoises are thriving: about 180,000 estimated on Aldabra
publications.text:
Giant tortoises are thriving: a new study estimates about 180,000 live on Aldabra Atoll in the Seychelles.

Aldabra is a ring of coral islands in the Indian Ocean and home to the largest free-roaming giant tortoise population in the world. The survey, led by the Seychelles Islands Foundation and the University of Exeter, analysed five years of tortoise counts from 2018 to 2022. It produced an estimate of approximately 180,000 tortoises, the highest figure ever recorded for the species. The study, published in Ecology and Evolution, found the population relatively stable.

In the 19th century, heavy exploitation left fewer than 1,000 tortoises on Aldabra. Since then the atoll has been protected, as a strict nature reserve since 1981 and a UNESCO site since 1982. The researchers say the new figure is a baseline for tracking the population in the future. Threats remain: longer and more frequent droughts, rising sea levels, and feral cats and black rats that prey on eggs and hatchlings.

Key facts:
• About 180,000 giant tortoises are estimated to live on Aldabra, an atoll in the Seychelles.
• It is the largest free-roaming giant tortoise population in the world.
• The once-endangered species is now described as thriving.
• Aldabra has been a strict nature reserve since 1981 and a UNESCO site since 1982.

publications.title: في جزيرة نائية بدولة سيشل، تعيش واحدة من أغرب الظواهر في عالم الحياة البرية؛
publications.text:
في جزيرة نائية بدولة سيشل، تعيش واحدة من أغرب الظواهر في عالم الحياة البرية؛ إذ كشف مسح علمي استمر خمس سنوات عن وجود نحو 180 ألف سلحفاة عملاقة في جزيرة ألدابرا، وهو عدد يتجاوز إجمالي سكان الدولة البالغ نحو 122 ألف نسمة!

لكن المدهش أن هذه السلاحف كانت على وشك الاختفاء تمامًا قبل نحو قرنين من الزمان. ففي القرن التاسع عشر، أدى الصيد الجائر على أيدي البحارة إلى تراجع أعدادها إلى أقل من ألف سلحفاة.

فكيف عادت بهذا العدد الهائل؟

السر كان في حماية السلاحف لسنوات طويلة، والحفاظ على موطنها الطبيعي، ومنع استنزاف أعدادها. ومع مرور العقود، استعادت هذه الكائنات موطئ قدمها، لتصبح ألدابرا اليوم موطنًا لأكبر تجمع للسلاحف العملاقة التي تعيش بحرية في العالم.

والسلاحف هنا ليست مجرد كائنات تعيش بأعداد ضخمة؛ فهي تؤدي دورًا مهمًا في الحفاظ على النظام البيئي، من خلال التأثير في نمو النباتات والمساعدة على نشر البذور.

ونُشرت نتائج التعداد الجديد في مجلة Ecology and Evolution، لتكشف عن تعافٍ لافت مقارنة بأواخر التسعينيات، حين قُدّر عدد السلاحف بنحو 100 ألف فقط.

من أقل من ألف سلحفاة إلى 180 ألفًا.. ألدابرا تقدم مثالًا مذهلًا على ما يمكن أن تحققه حماية الحياة البرية عندما تستمر لعقود.

#علوم_وصناعات #السلاحف_العملاقة #الحياة_البرية #حماية_البيئة

stories.title: Seychelles Company Suspected of Funding Nguesso Property Renovations
stories.description: According to the publication dated 24 October 2026, Julienne Nguesso and her husband Guy Johnson were placed under formal investigation in France in June 2017 over alleged money laundering and embezzlement connected to their 2006 purchase of a property in Neuilly-sur-Seine (France). Investigators reportedly suspect that public funds from Congo-Brazzaville were routed through offshore companies, including companies based in Seychelles, and that one Seychelles company helped finance part of the property’s renovations; these remain allegations.

publications.text:
Les Nguesso, une famille de paresseux qui ont fait de la politique leur profession pour se protéger des crimes financiers qu’ils commettent en République du Congo, une famille de voleurs qui ont mis le pays à sac.

Juliette Nguesso Issongo, comme son père Denis Sassou Nguesso, est poursuivie en France pour blanchiment et détournement de fonds publics.

La fille du tyran congolais, Denis Sassou Nguesso, Julienne Nguesso et son mari, Guy Johnson, ont été mis en examen en juin 2017. Ils sont poursuivis par la justice française pour des faits de blanchiment et de détournement de fonds publics, dans le cadre de l’enquête sur l’origine des fonds ayant permis au couple d’acheter, en 2006, via une SCI, un hôtel particulier à Neuilly-sur-Seine, dans la banlieue huppée de Paris. Le bien compte sept pièces et une piscine intérieure, selon une source proche du dossier.

À cet investissement d’un peu plus de 3 millions d’euros, l’équivalent d’environ 2 milliards de FCFA s’est ajoutée une facture de 5,34 millions d’euros (3.5 milliards de Fcfa) pour d’importants travaux réalisés entre 2007 et 2011.

Les enquêteurs, qui s’appuyaient sur des signalements de la cellule de lutte contre le blanchiment de Bercy, Tracfin, se sont intéressés à des mouvements financiers entre des banques de Saint-Marin et des sociétés étrangères.

D’après les investigations, plusieurs dizaines de millions d’euros provenant d’entités publiques du Congo-Brazzaville avaient été transférés, depuis 2007, sur les comptes de diverses sociétés offshore basées aux Seychelles, à l’île Maurice ou à Hong Kong. Ces sociétés sont soupçonnées de financer ensuite, en partie, le train de vie de certains membres du clan présidentiel, selon une source proche du dossier.

Les enquêteurs pensent que le couple a financé une partie des travaux par le biais d’une société seychelloise alimentée par le produit de la vente des parts détenues par Julienne Sassou-Nguesso dans une société de télécommunications. Cette dernière serait liée à des opérations de corruption, selon la même source.

stories.title: Annette Course Becomes First Woman Sergeant Major
stories.description: The Seychelles president (Patrick Herminie) welcomed Annette Course during a courtesy call with Commissioner of Police Godfra Hermitte after Course became the first woman to hold the Sergeant Major position in the Seychelles Police Force. The appointment was reported on 29 October 2026; Course has 19 years of service, and the date she assumed the role is not specified.

publications.text:
President Herminie Commends First Woman Sergeant Major in Historic Police Appointment

 President Dr Patrick Herminie welcomed Sergeant Major Annette Course, the first woman to hold the position in the Seychelles Police Force, during a courtesy call accompanied by Commissioner of Police Godfra Hermitte. 

With 19 years of service in the Seychelles Police Force, Sergeant Major Course has assumed responsibilities that include maintaining discipline, professional conduct and hygiene standards among police officers.

HISTORY IN THE MAKING

SEYCHELLES POLICE FORCE WELCOMES ITS FIRST FEMALE SERGEANT MAJOR

The Seychelles Police Force proudly announces the promotion of Annette Course to the rank of Sergeant Major, making her the first female officer in the Force’s history to attain this rank.

Having joined the Force on 1st  September 2007, Sergeant Major Course brings 19 years of dedicated service and experience. Throughout her career, she has served in various units and sections, including regular policing duties, Summon & warrant unit, VIC and Security Support Wings (SSU).

Her promotion is a significant step forward for gender equality and female representation in senior leadership within law enforcement. It demonstrates that dedication, professionalism and leadership are not defined by gender, while encouraging more women to pursue leadership opportunities in policing.

Sergeant Major Course’s achievement serves as an inspiration to female officers and young women aspiring to careers in law enforcement, reinforcing the importance of equal opportunities and recognising women’s contributions to public service.

The Seychelles Police Force congratulates Sergeant Major Annette Course on this well deserved promotion and wishes her every success in her new role.

A proud moment for the Force and an inspiring example of women breaking barriers in leadership.

publications.title: 77 police officers promoted as Seychelles Police Force names its first female Sergeant Major
publications.text:
77 police officers promoted as Seychelles Police Force names its first female Sergeant Major

Vice President Sebastien Pillay attended the official police promotion ceremony today, where he addressed 77 newly promoted officers on behalf of President Dr Patrick Herminie.

The officers were promoted to ranks ranging from Corporal to Chief Superintendent. The ceremony also marked a historic milestone, with Annette Course becoming the first female officer to be promoted to the rank of Sergeant Major. Sergeant Major Course brings 19 years of dedicated service and experience, having served in various units within the Seychelles Police Force.

In his address, Vice President Pillay reminded the officers that promotion comes with greater responsibilities, including the duty to serve without fear, favour or ill will. He expressed confidence in their ability to uphold the highest standards of professionalism and meet the expectations placed upon them.

Congratulating the officers on their accomplishments, the Vice President thanked them for their support, dedication and years of service to the Seychelles Police Force and the country.

The ceremony honoured the officers’ commitment and contributions, with particular recognition of those who have served for many years, reaffirming the commitment to ensuring that no officer is left behind.

publications.title: President Herminie Commends First Woman Sergeant Major in Historic Police Appointment
publications.text:
President Herminie Commends First Woman Sergeant Major in Historic Police Appointment

President Dr Patrick Herminie welcomed Sergeant Major Annette Course, the first woman to hold the position in the Seychelles Police Force, during a courtesy call accompanied by Commissioner of Police Godfra Hermitte.

With 19 years of service in the Seychelles Police Force, Sergeant Major Course has assumed responsibilities that include maintaining discipline, professional conduct and hygiene standards among police officers.

President Herminie congratulated Sergeant Major Course. on her historic achievement, wishing her courage and success as she assumes her responsibilities. He expressed confidence in her ability to contribute positively to strengthening standards within the police service.

During the meeting, the President reiterated the importance of exemplary conduct among police officers, stressing that restoring public trust and respect must remain a priority for the institution.

He emphasised that police officers have a responsibility to lead by example, noting that discipline, professionalism and proper conduct are fundamental to maintaining the confidence of the public.

The President also recalled his consistent message to the Commissioner of Police that officers must demonstrate exemplary behaviour in the discharge of their duties, highlighting the need to rebuild the respect that citizens should have for the police.

Sergeant Major Course expressed confidence in her ability to discharge her responsibilities effectively, drawing on the experience and knowledge gained throughout her 19 years of service.

Commissioner Hermitte welcomed the historic appointment, explaining that promoting women into leadership positions is among his objectives for the Seychelles Police Force. He emphasised the importance of creating opportunities for experienced and capable female officers to assume greater responsibilities within the institution.

The appointment of Sergeant Major Course represents an important step towards greater representation of women in police leadership, while reinforcing efforts to strengthen discipline and professional standards across the force.

Breaking Barriers in Police Leadership

History has been made in the Seychelles Police Force as Sergeant Major Annette Course becomes the first woman to occupy the position.

With 19 years of service, she takes on the responsibility of upholding discipline, professional conduct and hygiene standards within the force.

During a courtesy call at State House, President Dr Patrick Herminie congratulated Sergeant Major Course on her historic achievement, wishing her courage and success in her new role.

The President emphasised the importance of exemplary conduct among police officers, stressing the need to restore public trust and respect for the police.

Commissioner of Police Godfra Hermitte also highlighted his commitment to promoting more women into leadership positions within the force.

While global debate often centers on visa-free access, naturalization in Africa can require some of the world’s longest legal waiting periods.

Eritrea and Uganda require up to 20 years of continuous residency. Nigeria, Chad, and Seychelles require 15 years, plus proof of economic contributions, security clearance, and long term integration before granting full constitutional rights.

Mauritius authorities appeal for relatives of man believed to be Seychellois

Authorities in Mauritius are appealing to relatives of a man believed to be from Seychelles to claim his body, which has remained in a hospital mortuary for 21 months.

The man, identified as 64-year-old Frank Jeffrey Marie, reportedly died in an accident on New Truck Road in Roche-Bois on 3 January 2025.

His body has remained at the SSRN Hospital mortuary since his death, with no relatives coming forward to claim it.

Several Mauritians have since taken to social media, suggesting that Marie was originally from Seychelles.

His last known address in Mauritius was on Balisage Street.

It remains unclear whether Mauritian authorities have contacted the Seychelles High Commission over the matter.

stories.title: Police Search for Missing Man Off Anse Soleil (Seychelles)
stories.description: The publication says Seychelles police were searching for a missing man in waters off Anse Soleil (Seychelles). The search was reported in a Twitter post published on 2 November 2026; when the man went missing and his fate are not stated.

publications.text: Seychelles Police Search for Missing Man in Waters Off Anse Soleil #SeychellesNews https://t.co/FjQ5r5ILcY

POLICE STATEMENT (URGENT APPEAL)

The Seychelles Police are issuing an urgent appeal to the public, particularly families, urging anyone who has a missing family member to report the matter to the Police immediately.

The appeal follows an official report received by the Police late yesterday afternoon concerning a man who was riding a jet ski in the waters off Anse Soleil, Baie Lazare. The individual reportedly spotted what appeared to be the body of a man in the deeper waters.

According to the information provided, the person believed to be in the water was wearing a black wetsuit and had short hair.

Following the report, the Seychelles Coast Guard responded to provide assistance. This morning, the Marine Police launched a search operation in the waters stretching from Baie Lazare to Anse Boileau to verify the information received. However, no body has been located so far.

The Police confirm that, as of now, no official missing-person report has been received.

The Police are appealing to anyone who may have information that could assist with the investigation, or who has a family member currently missing, to contact the Police without delay.

Police Department
